ambiguities.evidence: The paper defines r_m as a computed value on printed p. 824, q_{m+1} as an exact residual on printed p. 825, and Lemma 4.2 bounds A(x_{m+1}-x) on printed p. 826. [PDF pp. 9-11, Section 4 algorithm, q-definition, and Lemma 4.2]
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract must keep these three quantities distinct; identifying any two would strengthen or alter the claim.
ambiguities.issue: The term "residual" can refer either to the exact residual image A(x_{m+1}-x), the exact intermediate residual q_{m+1}, or the computed residual r_m.

ambiguities.evidence: The loop is displayed for m=1,2,..., followed by x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1, while Lemma 4.2 begins at m=0. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, algorithm and initialization; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
ambiguities.impact: The base case should be represented separately or justified from those definitions.
ambiguities.issue: The m=0 case is covered through artificial initialization rather than the ordinary refinement loop.

ambiguities.evidence: The proof supplies only the abstract h_{m+1} componentwise bound and the standing well-defined-operation assumption. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof; PDF p. 3/printed 818, floating-point model]
ambiguities.impact: The contract cannot require IEEE-specific behavior beyond the stated error inequality.
ambiguities.issue: No machine-specific rounding mode is fixed.

contract_plain_english: For every m>=0, the exact residual of the computed next iterate is bounded componentwise by the exact residual before the rounded update, amplified by I+u|A||A^{-1}|, plus u|A||x|. The claim concerns exact residual images, not computed residual storage, and has no norm or big-O remainder. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 first inequality and proof]

source_evidence.observation: The paper treats Ax=b with n equations and n unknowns over a floating-point subset of the reals. Unit roundoff u is positive, nu <= .01, referenced floating-point results are assumed well-defined, and absolute values and inequalities are componentwise.
The exact solution is x=A^{-1}b in the column-pivoted Gaussian-elimination setting.
The algorithm obtains x_1 and d_m by column-pivoted solves and computes x_{m+1} by floating-point subtraction. It defines x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1 and considers both s.p.r.a. and d.p.r.a.

source_evidence.observation: q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b is the exact residual of the unrounded corrected value.

statement.algorithm_linkage: This is the first part of Lemma 4.2. It converts the exact intermediate residual q_{m+1} into a componentwise bound on the exact residual image of the rounded next iterate. It is not a bound on the computed residual r_{m+1}, a normwise residual estimate, or a convergence theorem. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 and proof]
binders: n is the system dimension; A is an n-by-n real matrix, b and x are n-vectors, and x=A^{-1}b. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 opening; PDF p. 8/printed 823, Section 3 basic-result paragraph]
u is the positive single-precision relative-roundoff bound, and I is the n-by-n identity matrix. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, floating-point model; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 first inequality]
conclusions: Componentwise, |A(x_{m+1}-x)| <= (I+u|A||A^{-1}|)|q_{m+1}| + u|A||x|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 first displayed inequality]
constants_and_indexing: The matrix coefficient is exactly I+u|A||A^{-1}|, and the additive term is exactly u|A||x|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, first displayed inequality]
The offset pairs q_{m+1} with x_{m+1}, for every m>=0. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
No anonymous C_i constant appears in this bound. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 first inequality]
definitions_and_conventions: Because Ax=b, A(x_{m+1}-x)=Ax_{m+1}-b is the exact residual of the computed iterate, not the separately computed residual r_{m+1}. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, x=A^{-1}b context; PDF p. 9/printed 824, r_m definition; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b is exact and refers to the unrounded corrected value. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition]
Vertical bars and inequalities are componentwise; |A||A^{-1}||q_{m+1}| and |A||x| are ordinary nonnegative matrix-vector products. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, componentwise convention]
The identity contribution I|q_{m+1}| and the rounding contribution u|A||A^{-1}||q_{m+1}| are both retained. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, first displayed inequality and proof]
error_notions: |A(x_{m+1}-x)|=|Ax_{m+1}-b| is a componentwise exact-residual magnitude for the computed iterate. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, exact-solution definition; PDF p. 11/printed 826, first inequality]
|q_{m+1}| is the componentwise magnitude of the exact residual before the rounded update. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition]
Neither side is the stored or computed residual r_m unless an additional equality not asserted by the paper is introduced. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, r_m definition; PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition]
exceptional_values: A must be nonsingular for A^{-1} to exist. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, x=A^{-1}b context]

Undefined floating-point results, overflow-like failures, and non-real exceptional values are excluded by the standing well-defined-real-operation assumption. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
Lemma 4.2 imposes no positivity or nonzero-component requirement on x or q_{m+1}. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
higher_order_terms: The inequality retains its full finite u-dependent expression and contains no O(u^2) or other omitted term. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 first inequality]
hypotheses: A is nonsingular, inherited from x=A^{-1}b and the repeated use of A^{-1}. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, Section 3 basic-result paragraph]
The iterates and corrections are those of column-pivoted iterative refinement, including x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1 for m=0. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm definition]
The rounded update satisfies x_{m+1}=x_m-d_m+h_{m+1} with |h_{m+1}| <= u|x_m-d_m|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]
All referenced floating-point operations are well-defined. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
No conditioning or smallness hypothesis beyond the standing floating-point context is stated for Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
implicit_context: The claim is within Section 4's column-pivoted iterative-refinement analysis. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm definition]

Both s.p.r.a. and d.p.r.a. are in scope; the claim is independent of which precision was used to accumulate r_m because it is derived only from q_{m+1} and the final update. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, precision paragraph; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]
At m=0, q_1=Ax_1-b under x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, initialization; PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition]
norms: No norm occurs in the conclusion; it is a vector inequality interpreted componentwise. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, componentwise convention; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 first inequality]
numerical_model: The standing single-precision model has relative-roundoff bound u and nu <= .01, with operations assumed well-defined. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
The proof's explicit rounding model is |h_{m+1}| <= u|x_m-d_m| for the final subtraction. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]

Single- and double-precision residual accumulation differ in forming r_m, but no residual-precision parameter occurs in this claim. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, residual-precision paragraph; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]

undebatable_constraints: The quantified range is every integer m>=0. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
The claim is componentwise and vector-valued, not normwise. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, componentwise convention; PDF p. 11/printed 826, first inequality]
The left side is |A(x_{m+1}-x)|, equivalently the exact residual |Ax_{m+1}-b|. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, exact x; PDF p. 11/printed 826, first inequality]
The right side uses the exact intermediate residual q_{m+1}, not the computed residual r_m. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, r_m definition; PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition]
The full coefficient I+u|A||A^{-1}| and the additive u|A||x| term must both be preserved. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, first displayed inequality]
The source result is shared by the s.p.r.a. and d.p.r.a. variants of column-pivoted iterative refinement. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm and precision paragraph]
